title: Your Agent Failed in Prod. Good Luck Reproducing It. - Tisha Chawla & Susheem Koul, Microsoft
talk_summary: The talk argues that bitwise determinism from hosted LLM APIs is unattainable (batch invariance, MoE routing, float non-associativity), so teams should instead record every node boundary's input/output plus metadata to make runs replayable and debuggable. Their 'Chronicle' prototype annotates methods as boundaries, records traces, then replays them with all-but-one node stubbed so a fixed guardrail/tool can be tested deterministically and for free.

takeaways.what_they_do: Wrap each agent node (LLM call, tool, retrieval) in a boundary annotation that records input/output plus model version, sampling params, and build ID, so a failed prod run becomes a frozen trace.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Record at the boundary instead because you need to capture what enters each node and what leaves it.

takeaways.technique: Replay with selective stubbing as free regression tests
takeaways.what_they_do: Load a recorded trace, stub every node except the one changed, run live only that node, and assert on its output — no model calls needed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you stub every node other than the node that you changed, and you let Boundary handle the rest
takeaways.numbers: replay 'never calls the model, it is free'

takeaways.technique: Guardrails at tool boundaries, tested via replay
takeaways.what_they_do: Since the LLM can't be made deterministic, put validation guardrails on tool calls and verify them by replaying the exact failing trace with the tool live.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can put guardrails on your tools to enforce some level of uh credibility on your production agent

takeaways.what_they_do: Deterministic nodes (tools, guardrails) get replay-based tests; subjective properties (tone, trajectory) get LLM-as-judge.
takeaways.evidence_quote: There's the deterministic testing, and then the behavioral testing.

takeaways.technique: Log the full envelope, not just the prompt
takeaways.what_they_do: Record model version, sampling params, RAG chunks, and build ID alongside prompt/response so the whole state of a run is frozen.
takeaways.evidence_quote: capture the full envelope. Don't focus on just the prompt.

takeaways.what_they_do: Argue temperature zero is not truly deterministic on hosted GPUs/MoE and pinning it just repeats the same logical error; keep generation variation and rely on replay instead.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Setting the temperature to zero doesn't fix a broken reasoning path.
takeaways.numbers: same prompt run 1000 times can return 'dozens of completely different responses'
